concept.title: Opening up the Process to Appeals

conbody.p: Because of the CASE Act’s goal to make the process of copyright litigation speedier, the ability to appeal must be made available to the losing party. While the inability to appeal has been justified by the presence of a three-person tribunal rather than one deciding judge, there is still potential for bias, particularly if those appointed previously primarily represented holders rather than consumers. Because the world of copyright litigation is often fueled and funded by the big names of the entertainment industry, and those selected for the board are in some part required to have decent experience in copyright, the potential for biased selection is strong. Providing the losing party with the ability to appeal would ensure that even if the board is biased against the defendant, there remains a safeguard to stop overreach.
